research_question: Among people with cancer receiving anticancer therapy, what is the effect of resistance training, compared with no training, on cancer-related fatigue measured at 12 weeks or less?
treatment_label: Resistance training delivered during anticancer therapy
control_label: No exercise training or usual care without a structured training program
outcome_description: Cancer-related fatigue assessed with any validated self-report, clinician-rated, or performance-related fatigue instrument at a post-baseline assessment occurring no later than 12 weeks after the start of the intervention. If multiple eligible assessments are reported within 12 weeks, extract the prespecified primary endpoint or, if none is specified, the assessment closest to 12 weeks. Fatigue outcomes measured only after 12 weeks are outside this analysis.
positive_direction: A positive standardized mean difference means resistance training reduced cancer-related fatigue more than no training/usual care and therefore favors resistance training.
search_queries: cancer resistance training fatigue controlled trial
anticancer therapy resistance exercise fatigue experiment
oncology strength training cancer-related fatigue quantitative comparison
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies of people with any cancer type receiving anticancer therapy that evaluate a resistance-training intervention, alone or as the principal distinguishable exercise component.
Studies containing a no-training, non-exercise, wait-list, attention-control, or usual-care comparison condition.
Studies reporting a quantitative measure of cancer-related fatigue at an eligible post-baseline time point of 12 weeks or less.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study; systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, protocols without results, and theoretical papers are excluded.
No comparison between a resistance-training treatment condition and a no-training or otherwise eligible control condition.

No quantitative fatigue outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as means and standard deviations, t/F-values, proportions, or odds ratios, and the required data cannot be obtained or derived.
Completely unrelated to resistance training during anticancer therapy and cancer-related fatigue, or reports fatigue only at follow-up windows later than 12 weeks.
moderators_to_extract: Resistance-training dose and format, including frequency, intensity, duration, supervision, and whether resistance training was standalone or part of a multicomponent program
Outcome timing within the eligible 12-week window
effect_size_note: Pool eligible continuous fatigue outcomes as standardized mean differences. Harmonize scoring direction before analysis so that positive effects consistently indicate less fatigue with resistance training; apply the small-sample correction if the synthesis software reports Hedges-adjusted SMDs. Do not combine measurements taken after 12 weeks with this outcome.
